news.title: Democratic super PAC’s spending in Indian-American Shah, Dandiya races tops $18 million
news.text: Digital Desk | Atlanta, Oct 30 (IANS) House Majority PAC, the main Democratic super PAC focused on the US House, has now reported spending more than $18 million in the races of Indian American Democrats Amish Shah in Arizona and Pia Dandiya in Florida, according to a review of Federal Election Commission filings. The group’s latest 24-hour report, signed on October 28 and covering spending dated October 27, puts its running total in Florida’s 22nd congressional district at $12,098,456.27 and in Arizona’s 1st district at $6,384,915.45, a combined $18,483,371.72. The single day of spending added about $6.09 million across the two races. In Florida, the PAC reported $3,534,624 for television advertising against Republican Casey Askar, $339,120 for radio, $184,736 for digital ads and $54,930.88 for mail, along with $11,250 in digital ads supporting Dandiya. In Arizona, it reported $1,911,519.65 for television ads against Republican Tom Feely and $58,008 for digital advertising. Shah, a physician and former Arizona state legislator, is running in a Phoenix-area seat. The previous report, filed a day earlier, had put the FL-22 total at $7,973,795.39 and the AZ-1 total at $4,415,387.80. The Republican side has also escalated in Florida. No Going Back PAC, a super PAC funded by MAGA Inc., the main outside group backing President Donald Trump, reported two more television buys against Dandiya through MHB Media: $1,516,950 dated October 26 and $1,450,800 dated October 28. That brings its total spending against her to $9,450,178.72, according to its filing. Dandiya, meanwhile, reported raising $102,144.75 from 49 contributions on October 26 and 27 in a pre-election 48-hour notice. Donors included the Communications Workers of America’s political arm, the United Auto Workers’ V-CAP and Innovation for Good PAC, at $5,000 each, as well as campaign committees of sitting Democratic lawmakers. Arizona’s 1st district has drawn about $25.4 million in outside spending since the July primary, the most of any House race in the state, Phoenix broadcaster KTAR reported. The spending figures come from self-reported electronic filings that have not yet been processed by the FEC and could be amended. Super PAC totals listed on each report are cumulative for the race, and the figures for media buys are often estimates. Both seats are Democratic targets in the November 3 midterm elections. The scale of outside money makes the two contests among the most expensive involving Indian American candidates this cycle. Shah and Dandiya are both children of immigrants from India.

news.title: Crypto exchange Binance freezes assets after $6.3 billion security breach
news.text:
Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a security breach had resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact that analysts said could amount to the biggest crypto heist ever and might make investors rethink the risks of owning digital assets.

Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3 billion as Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover “all hacking losses”.

An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of its engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said.

Markets reacted immediately in early Asian trading on Friday.

Bitcoin dropped more than 3 per cent to a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3pc to a two-month low of $2,178. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5pc over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.

Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8pc while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy fell nearly 6pc in extended US trading.

The incident could be the world’s biggest crypto heist, according to analytics firm Chainalysis and other industry experts.

“It’s the biggest hack in history,” said Aravind Srinivasan, head of large crypto market maker GSR’s systematic OTC business.

Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure lately due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.

“It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges, as well as counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks,” said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong.

Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange’s 2025 annual report.

“User funds remain safe,” Binance said in a statement.

“As a precaution, all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while our security teams conduct checks, secure wallet infrastructure, and trace affected assets, with the close support of our law enforcement and industry partners.”

Binance has secure asset fund

Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, which is a reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website.

“It’s becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them,” said Bernardo Brites, CEO of Trace Finance, a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company.

“My view is that users will move away from smaller and medium-sized exchanges, (it is) becoming too risky to park your money somewhere that couldn’t cover a hack of meaningful size.”

Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.

World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said on Thursday it had worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack. Binance’s Yi said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.

Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and was freezing affected funds and coordinating with relevant parties.

Incident adds to string of crypto thefts

Miguel Morel, CEO of blockchain intelligence firm Arkham, said data indicated that billions of dollars appeared to have been hacked from Binance by an unknown actor.

The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry’s vulnerability to hackers.

Authorities have warned that organised crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system.

Binance.US, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was not affected by the security incident.

Coinbase said it was unaffected and was monitoring the situation.

In an unrelated incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market operator Polymarket temporarily halted trading after a security incident involving a third-party provider. It later resumed trading and said it would fully reimburse affected traders.

news.title: Trump links oil price relief to Iran outcome
news.text: Digital Desk | Washington, Oct 30 (IANS) US President Donald Trump said oil prices would fall sharply once his administration ensured Iran could not acquire a nuclear weapon, linking relief for households facing high fuel costs to the outcome of the confrontation with Tehran. In an interview with WHNS-TV, Trump predicted that the situation would be resolved soon. He offered no specific timetable or details of how that objective would be achieved. “They will never have a nuclear weapon. So, that's going to be over with soon,” he said. “And as soon as that's over with, the oil prices will come plummeting.” Trump was responding to a question about families struggling with high petrol and grocery prices. The interviewer asked what policies would bring prices down and how long households would have to wait. The president said oil prices were already declining and forecast a much steeper fall. He argued that other prices had also fallen substantially, while pointing to economic growth and stock market gains as evidence that his policies were working. “They just announced, for the last three months, 1.7 percent inflation,” Trump said. He did not identify the inflation measure or explain the calculation in the interview. His remarks also did not specify how much he expected fuel prices to fall or when consumers would see the promised relief. At a separate rally in Rock Hill, South Carolina, Trump repeated his prediction of lower oil and petrol prices while defending his administration’s approach to Iran. He also floated the idea of renaming the Strait of Hormuz after himself. “I'm thinking about calling the Hormuz Strait, the Trump Strait,” he told supporters. The remark came during a passage in which he discussed changing geographical names. He did not announce a formal proposal or describe steps to implement such a change. Trump also pointed to Venezuela as a source of additional oil supplies. In the television interview, he said the United States was receiving millions of barrels from the country each week following what he described as a swift military victory. “We're taking in millions of barrels of oil from Venezuela every single week,” he said. He did not provide shipment figures or contractual details in the interview. At the Rock Hill rally, Trump linked his broader economic promises to the midterm election outcome. He pledged a $5,000 payment to every adult US citizen if Republicans won both chambers of Congress. “If Republicans win the House of Representatives and the US Senate, I am going to give all adult citizens in the United States of America $5,000, very easily.” Trump said recipients would have to spend the money within the United States. He put the cost at approximately $1 trillion and cited tariff revenue and economic performance in support of the pledge. He did not set out a payment timetable or detailed funding plan. The president also credited tariffs with encouraging companies to manufacture in America. Trump’s South Carolina appearances centred on support for Darline Graham’s Senate campaign. During the rally, he urged supporters to vote early and treat the congressional elections as a verdict on his administration, even though he was not personally on the ballot. The economic measures he promoted included provisions in the legislation he calls the One Big Beautiful Bill. In the interview, he highlighted tax relief involving tips, overtime, seniors and car-loan interest, describing the package as central to his economic agenda for the remainder of his term.

news.title: Desi Playbook in US Polls: How India’s ‘Dummy Candidate’ Trick Found Its Way into the Midterms
news.text: Few people in India will recall that in the 2014 Lok Sabha elections Hema Malini contested against Hema Malini in Mathura. Or that in 2019, Rahul Gandhi was pitted against another Rahul Gandhi, and even a Raghul Gandhi, in Wayanad.These dummy candidates might be commonplace in India and might even provide comic relief to our gruelling electoral drama. But thousands of miles away, a similar dummy candidate in a remote part of the United States - in Alaska - has triggered a political firestorm ahead of the crucial mid-term elections that will virtually be a referendum on President Donald Trumps policies and popularity.And Trump is milking the controversy, apparently triggered by the Democrats dirty tricks department, to his maximum advantage. According to almost all opinion polls, Trumps Republican Party is trailing nationwide in the Nov. 3 elections for the House of Representatives and the Senate, the two chambers of Congress or parliament, including in Republican strongholds like Alaska.In that detached-from-the-mainland state, Republican candidate for Senate, incumbent Daniel Sullivan, is facing a tough fight against Democrat candidate Mary Peltola. As if that was not enough, a third candidate on the ballot is also named Daniel Sullivan, a retired schoolteacher.That in itself was not a big deal until the New York Times reported on Wednesday that the teacher Sullivans candidature was the result of a coordinated effort by Peltolas team. Immediately, Trump cried foul and ordered a Justice Department investigation into alleged voter fraud.The Trump administrations contention is that the Alaska Democrats sought to confuse voters by recruiting a dummy candidate to siphon votes from the Republican Sullivan. This is Voter Fraud at the Highest Level ... this behavior in our Elections cannot be allowed to continue, Trump wrote on Truth Social, and called for Peltola to be removed from the ballot and prosecuted.On Thursday, CNN reported that the Justice Department has dramatically accelerated a criminal probe into the case, issuing dozens of new grand jury subpoenas and homing in on new potential charges. On the face of it, there is nothing illegal about a candidate of the same name entering the ballot.The ballot paper itself identifies the two Sullivans clearly - one as the incumbent and the other with no party affiliation. But Trump has spent years spinning false conspiracies about Democratic cheating and non-existent electoral fraud. Now, at last he has a data point to sculpt into a suggestive narrative, wrote CNNs political analyst Stephen Collinson. And whether the OG (original) Dan Sullivan wins or loses, the president will be sure to highlight shenanigans in Alaska to claim Democrats everywhere are corrupt - especially if the GOP bombs on Tuesday (Nov. 3), he wrote.However, under US laws, elections are a state matter and it is up to the state to decide who enters the ballot and the Federal government has no say in it. The Justice Department probe therefore may not stand up in court. But in politics, as opposed to the law, perception has long been as important as reality.Trump understands this more instinctively than any modern president, wrote Collinson. If Trump appears desperate to mount what could be a frivolous legal challenge, he has good reason to: it would be disastrous for him if the Republicans lose control of the 100-member Senate on top of a most likely loss in the House of Representatives. The Senate is hanging in the balance and a handful of states, including Alaska, will decide the outcome. A New York Times Sienna poll gave the Democrats a 51 to 45 per cent lead over Sullivan. If Alaska ends up deciding which party controls the Senate, expect major chaos as Trump will not give up without a massive fight.In India too, a legal challenge was mounted in 2024 against double/duplicate/namesake/impostor/dupe candidates in the form of a public interest litigation. But the learned judges of the Supreme Court gave it a short shrift, saying somebodys name, whether Rahul Gandhi or Lalu Prasad Yadav, cannot come in the way of their right to contest elections.The master of dummy candidates in India was Ajit Jogi of the Congress party. In 2014, faced against BJPs Chandulal Sahu in Mahsamund in Chhattisgarh, Jogi managed to gather at least seven other Chandulals to contest against the real Sahu. Three more were Chandurams. Still, the BJPs Sahu won by a narrow margin even though the others also got a sizeable number of votes. For the record, Hema Malini lost the 2014 elections. Not the actress; the other one.

news.title: Iowa GOP Congressional Candidate Joe Mitchell Eyes House Oversight Seat to ‘Investigate the Hell Out of Anthony Fauci’
news.text:
Clive, Iowa — Republican Iowa congressional candidate Joe Mitchell vowed to investigate former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases Director Dr. Anthony Fauci if elected to Congress, expressing his desire to serve on an oversight committee while recounting his grandmother’s death following a COVID-19 vaccination during a Make Iowa Healthy Again rally Wednesday.

MAHA PAC hosted the October 28 “Get Out the Vote Rally” in Clive, Iowa, a suburb of Des Moines, ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Speakers included Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Republican Iowa gubernatorial candidate Zach Lahn, Republican congressional candidate Joe Mitchell, and other Republican candidates, elected officials, and health, consumer, and agricultural advocates.

“My grandmother, who was 93 years old in 2022. She was a very healthy 93-year-old, by the way,” Mitchell said. “And we send her to a nursing home. This is several years after COVID. We send her to a nursing home, and they give her the COVID vaccine. Without anybody’s consent.”

“And they said there was a mandate here in the nursing home, so she went from a perfectly healthy 93-year-old to dead within two weeks,” he continued.

“Within two weeks, and so this is where the story of MAHA is personal to me because I don’t know about you, but I’m not a big fan of Anthony Fauci. Are you?” Mitchell asked, prompting members of the crowd to shout “no.”

“And I just talked to a member of Congress who’s on one of the steering committees, and she said, ‘When you’re elected next Tuesday, which committees would you like to be on?'” Mitchell recounted.

“And I said, ‘I want to be on oversight because I want to investigate the hell out of Anthony Fauci for what he did to this country,'” Mitchell declared, drawing cheers from the audience, with some attendees standing in response.

Mitchell said MAHA Action endorsed only 13 candidates nationwide, including himself and Republican Iowa gubernatorial candidate Zach Lahn, before explaining what he believes contributed to his endorsement.

“Part of the reason was I’m the only Republican in the entire country running for Congress who’s not going to be taking corporate PAC money in D.C. Not a single dime,” Mitchell said.

“So that means no money from BlackRock, no money from Pfizer, no money from Cisco, no money from these huge multinational corporations that have been running Washington for years,” he continued.

“And for me, that was a big pillar of my campaign because I said there’s too many politicians in Washington specifically that are bought and paid for, and they’re bought and paid for by big pharma, big ag, big food, and we don’t want those people dictating our lives anymore,” Mitchell said.

Mitchell’s remarks come as Republican lawmakers continue calling for accountability over Fauci’s handling of the COVID-19 pandemic. In August, Sen. Ron Johnson (R-WI) called for a “COVID reckoning,” accusing Fauci of helping fund gain-of-function research that may have contributed to the pandemic, covering up COVID-19’s origins, and promoting COVID-19 vaccines, while declaring, “I want to make sure that Anthony Fauci’s reputation is completely destroyed.” 

Rep. Brandon Gill (R-TX) similarly accused Fauci and other officials of withholding information from Americans, stating, “People’s lives were ruined with this, and these people ought to be held accountable,” and adding, “I want to see this guy go to jail.” Sen. Rand Paul (R-KY), chairman of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, also argued that Fauci could face charges for “lying to Congress” and “destroying records,” although he acknowledged that those alleged offenses were covered by former President Joe Biden’s pardon.

Mitchell, a former Iowa state representative endorsed by President Donald Trump, is facing Democrat state Rep. Lindsay James in the November 3 general election for Iowa’s 2nd Congressional District. The seat is currently held by Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-IA), who is running for the U.S. Senate. Trump endorsed Mitchell on January 27, highlighting his previous service at the Department of Housing and Urban Development during his administration and his distinction as the youngest state legislator in Iowa history. “Joe has proven he has the Courage and Wisdom to deliver strong results for the incredible people of his wonderful State and Nation,” Trump wrote.

Mitchell has also characterized James as being “Left, FAR Left.” “If you think it’s okay to use our taxpayer dollars to pay for a sex change for a prisoner, you shouldn’t be dealing with healthcare, you shouldn’t be dealing with education, you shouldn’t be dealing with our tax policy, you shouldn’t be involved in politics as far as I’m concerned,” he stated.

James previously apologized for being a white woman on her 2020 Iowa state legislative campaign website, as Breitbart News reported in June. In a section titled “A Confession,” James wrote, “I am a white, cis-gender, able bodied, middle class, college educated woman,” adding, “There is no doubt that I have worked hard to get where I am in my life, but I have also benefited greatly from privilege.”

During an interview, James was asked whether she considered someone living in Iowa to be an Iowan “regardless of immigration status.” “Yeah! I am all about making sure people have healthcare and resources they need,” James responded.

During a March 2023 interview concerning legislation banning puberty blockers, hormone therapies, and gender-transition surgeries for children under 18, James said, “Every evidence-based U.S. medical society affirms that gender affirming care is medically necessary and can be lifesaving.” “No one wants a politician making private medical decisions that parents and kids should be making with their doctors,” James added. James also voted against the legislation, which was signed into law in 2023. 

She voted against a 2022 bill restricting participation in female school sports to biological females and legislation requiring school bathrooms to correspond with students’ biological sex.

In 2025, James voted against SF 418, which prohibited instruction on gender identity theories in kindergarten through sixth grade, removed gender identity as a protected class under the Iowa Civil Rights Act, and established a statutory definition of sex as male or female. She has also voted against legislation requiring parental notification when students sought to change their gender at school.

During an October debate with Mitchell, a moderator repeatedly pressed James to explain why she missed 177 of 342 Iowa House votes since launching her congressional campaign, more than half of the votes taken during that period. James did not directly answer the questions, according to Townhall. Among the votes she missed in April and May were measures concerning property tax reductions, strengthening criminal penalties for animal torture, and limiting screen time in public schools. Townhall reported that James missed those votes while hosting campaign events across Iowa’s 2nd Congressional District.

James has also opposed major Republican tax legislation, voting against Iowa’s 2022 income tax overhaul, which established a 3.9 percent flat income tax. At the federal level, she called for repealing the Working Families Tax Cuts in September, following her May statement that lawmakers needed to “undo the OBBB.”

Republican Iowa congressional candidate Joe Mitchell vowed to investigate former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases Director Dr. Anthony Fauci if elected to Congress, expressing his desire to serve on an oversight committee while recounting his grandmother's death following a COVID-19 vaccination during a Make Iowa Healthy Again rally Wednesday.

news.title: Jeffries on Impeachment: We 'Haven't Ruled Anything Out'
news.text:
Thursday on “ABC News Live,” House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) spoke with ABC News correspondent Jay O’Brien regarding the possible impeachment of President Donald Trump.

Jeffries said, “The American people are clearly poised to give House and Senate Democrats a chance to govern on their behalf, and to fight to actually make life more affordable. We have gained the trust advantage.”

O’Brien said, “But is that just because they don’t trust the president?”

Jeffries said, “No. Well, I think we’ve gained the trust advantage, Democrats, as compared to Republicans, on a whole host of issues.”

He added, “We’re going to have to work as hard as we can to make sure that we are relentlessly pushing to end this affordability crisis, because the American people are sending that message.”

O’Brien said, “Some of your members have openly talked about, over the course of these campaigns, impeaching the president. Is that something voters want?”

Jeffries said, “Well, it’s very interesting because I actually have not heard, coming from House Democrats, a lot of talk about impeachment. In fact, what we have talked about is accountability more broadly defined. And we believe that it is important for Congress to function as a check and balance on an out-of-control executive branch.”

O’Brien said, “But would impeachment be a distraction from the work you’re trying to do?”

Jeffries said, “Well, we haven’t ruled anything in, and we haven’t ruled anything out, because we’ve made clear that we’re focused on addressing the affordability crisis.”

Listen to this article Share Spain train crash audio raises questions over control centre decisions Leaked audio recordings have raised fresh questions about the decisions made by Spain’s railway control centre shortly before a high speed train collision that killed 69 people near Urda.

The recordings, published by Spanish media, capture exchanges between train drivers and the Madrid control centre minutes before the crash. They appear to show that a train travelling from Madrid to Seville was cleared to move despite another train having stopped on the track ahead.

Authorities are investigating the cause of the disaster, one of Europe’s deadliest rail accidents in recent decades. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has pledged a thorough investigation, while King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visited injured passengers in hospital.

The Renfe train involved was carrying 397 passengers, while the stationary train, operated by private company Iryo, had 147 on board. Spain has begun three days of national mourning as investigators examine a reported automatic signalling failure and the decisions that preceded the collision.

Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot and Arab party leaders have accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s allies of trying to undermine the election result after his coalition lost its parliamentary majority.

Netanyahu’s Likud party alleged that Arab-led parties had benefited from bribery and possible foreign interference, prompting an investigation by Israel’s Shin Bet security agency into suspected illegal funding from Qatar and Turkey. Qatar has rejected the allegations as dangerous and baseless.

Final results gave Netanyahu’s bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, against 48 for Eisenkot’s bloc. The Joint List and Ra’am, two Arab-led political groupings, won a combined 19 seats after a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

Netanyahu’s critics say the allegations could be intended to make cooperation between Eisenkot’s bloc and Arab parties politically difficult. Such an alliance could provide the opposition with its only viable route to forming a governing majority.

Alphabet, Google’s parent company, lost more than $500 billion in market value on Thursday as investors reacted to concerns that artificial intelligence could undermine its core search advertising business.

The company’s shares fell to a six-month low after its latest results raised questions about the impact of AI-generated search summaries on advertising sales. Alphabet’s market value dropped to about $3.46 trillion from $3.97 trillion a day earlier.

Revenue rose 25 percent year on year to $127.6 billion, supported by Google Cloud, where revenue more than doubled to nearly $31 billion. However, quarterly profit fell 25 percent, while Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of more than $9 billion.

The sell-off reflects wider investor concerns about the cost of the AI race, with Microsoft and Amazon also planning substantial spending. Investors are increasingly questioning whether heavy investment in AI can sustain growth without weakening established businesses that generate much of the companies’ revenue.

At least 14 people have been killed and several others injured after a Russian drone struck a crowded railway platform in Dnipro, central Ukraine, according to local officials.

Regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 14 people were wounded, including an 11-year-old boy. Ukraine’s state railway operator said a passenger train travelling to Zaporizhzhia was at the platform when the drone hit.

Railway officials said a heightened threat level had been announced before the attack, but many people remained at the station. President Volodymyr Zelensky said the drone struck a platform where commuter and passenger trains were standing and called for further sanctions against Russia.

Russia has repeatedly attacked Ukraine’s railway network, although Moscow denies deliberately targeting civilians. Separately, a Russian missile strike in Chernihiv killed two 15-year-old girls and injured at least 25 others, according to regional officials.

More than 43 million Americans have cast ballots ahead of the US midterm elections, with early voting running at a pace that could surpass participation in previous congressional elections.

Data from the University of Florida Election Lab showed that four to five million votes were being cast daily in the run-up to election day. Political analysts have also reported unusually high turnout in Texas and among Hispanic voters.

Texas has recorded more than 5.8 million early votes, around 1.75 million above its total at the same stage in 2022. The state is a key battleground in the contest for control of the Senate and could help determine the balance of power during President Donald Trump’s term.

In states that record voters’ party affiliations, Democrats accounted for 44 percent of early ballots, compared with 31.2 percent for Republicans and 24.7 percent for voters without a declared party affiliation. The figures cover only states that collect such data and do not establish how unaffiliated voters intend to vote.

Ethiopia has received 12 Su-35 fighter jets from Russia as fighting intensifies in the northern Tigray region, raising concerns about wider regional security tensions.

Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed described the acquisition as a milestone for Ethiopia’s defence capabilities, saying the deal had been agreed several years ago and the aircraft arrived ahead of schedule. He also announced plans to acquire four S-400 air defence systems from Moscow.

Abiy said the equipment would help protect Ethiopia against external threats, including risks to major cities and critical infrastructure such as the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam. Military intelligence analyst Qalaab Segatu said the purchase indicated that Ethiopia was preparing for possible conflicts beyond its internal security challenges.

The acquisition deepens military cooperation between Ethiopia and Russia, which signed agreements in recent years covering military training and technology. The deal comes amid heightened tensions in the Horn of Africa, including Ethiopia’s strained relations with neighbouring Eritrea.

Twenty-seven Ugandan nationals recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine have been killed or are presumed dead, according to a diplomatic letter from Uganda’s embassy in Moscow.

The letter, seen by Reuters, listed 11 Ugandans confirmed dead and 16 whose bodies could not be located, including among prisoners of war. Uganda’s foreign ministry confirmed the document was authentic, while Russia’s embassy in Kampala did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Reports of African nationals being recruited to fight for Russia have increased, with some reportedly promised civilian jobs before being sent to the front lines. The cases have triggered concern in countries including Kenya, Ghana and South Africa.

Ukraine said last year that more than 1,400 people from about three dozen African countries were fighting alongside Russian forces. Moscow has denied illegally recruiting African citizens, as governments across the continent face growing pressure to investigate recruitment networks and protect their nationals.

Three bodies have been recovered after an offshore drilling rig operated by Borr Drilling sank off the coast of Gabon, with two people still missing.

The Prospector 5 rig went down on Saturday near the southern coastal town of Mayumba. Gabon’s navy said the bodies were found on Wednesday, while Borr Drilling confirmed that recovery operations were continuing.

The company said 110 of the 115 people aboard had been accounted for by Monday, leaving five missing. The three bodies were located with the assistance of an underwater remotely operated vehicle.

The rig had been contracted to support drilling operations for BW Energy but had not begun drilling at the time of the incident. Authorities and the company are continuing recovery efforts as questions remain over the circumstances surrounding the sinking.

Moroccan pharmaceutical company Laprophan has secured regulatory approval for an initial public offering on the Casablanca Stock Exchange, seeking to raise 2.22 billion dirhams, or about $230 million.

The offering will combine the issuance of 4.1 million new shares with the sale of up to 2.41 million existing shares by current shareholders. The subscription price has been set at 341 dirhams per share, according to the prospectus published by the market regulator.

The subscription period is scheduled to run from November 9 to 17. The capital increase will provide the company with additional funding, while the sale of existing shares will allow current investors to reduce their holdings.

The listing adds a pharmaceutical company to Morocco’s public equity market as businesses seek access to capital through share sales. The outcome will depend on investor demand during the subscription period.

South Africa has selected Durban as its leading candidate to host the 2036 or 2040 Summer Olympic and Paralympic Games, with organisers considering a multi-city bid.

Lwandile Simelane, acting president of the South African Sports Confederation, Olympic and Paralympic Committee, announced the choice on Thursday. She said events could also be held in other cities, including Johannesburg and Cape Town.

Durban, a coastal city of about four million people, was previously considered as a possible Olympic host following South Africa’s successful staging of the 2010 FIFA World Cup. An official bid did not materialise at the time, partly because of concerns about the costs involved.

The International Olympic Committee is expected to select the host city for the 2036 Games in mid-2029. South Africa’s proposed bid would place the country back in contention to stage one of the world’s largest sporting events, although funding, infrastructure and the distribution of events across cities will be important considerations.

news.title: ‘LA’s Mamdani’ eyes mayor’s office, but her fellow socialists stand in the way
news.text: With just days remaining before Los Angeles elects its next mayor, City Councilmember Nithya Raman is preparing for the possibility of leading America's second-largest city. But the socialist organization that helped launch her political career has issued an ultimatum: If she wants to retain its support, she must explicitly endorse a boycott of Israel. Her willingness to describe the boycott movement as a legitimate form of protest against what she calls genocide in Gaza is no longer enough. The demand comes from the national leadership of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), the organization that also helped propel Zohran Mamdani to the New York City mayor's office. On Monday, its National Political Committee approved two resolutions that could lead to the withdrawal of its endorsement of Raman and, ultimately, her expulsion from the organization. By Saturday, October 31, Raman is expected to clarify her position on a series of questions concerning Israel and the Palestinians. The demands include explicit support for the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement, avoiding ties with organizations the DSA classifies as Zionist lobbying groups, and opposing the transfer of funds to Israel and organizations such as the Jewish National Fund. The national leadership is also seeking a commitment from Raman to oppose weapons shipments to Israel through Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), even though the authority of a municipal government to restrict such international shipments is limited. If elected, Raman would face another deadline. Unless she expresses support for BDS and opposition to weapons shipments by January 1, the DSA plans to initiate disciplinary proceedings that could ultimately result in her expulsion. The dispute has created a complication for Raman's campaign as the mayoral race tightens. A UC Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies poll, conducted with the Los Angeles Times and released Wednesday, found Raman and incumbent Mayor Karen Bass tied at 40% support each, with 19% of likely voters undecided. Just a month earlier, Raman had held an 11-point lead. Bass, a former longtime member of Congress, has faced growing dissatisfaction over homelessness, the cost of living and criticism of her handling of the devastating January 2025 wildfires, which erupted while she was visiting Ghana. On Israel, however, Bass has taken a markedly different position from her challenger. At a September forum with Los Angeles' Jewish community, she rejected the characterization of Israel's actions in Gaza as genocide and said she would oppose municipal legislation promoting a boycott of Israel. She also emphasized her commitment to combating antisemitism and protecting Jewish institutions. From opposing BDS to including it in her platform of protest Raman, 45, has an unusual political biography even without the controversy surrounding Israel. Born in the Indian state of Kerala, she immigrated to the United States with her family at age six, studied at Harvard University and earned a master's degree in urban planning from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. She worked in the nonprofit sector, co-founded an organization assisting homeless people in Los Angeles and, in 2020, defeated an incumbent City Council member, the first successful challenge of its kind in the city in 17 years. She became the first South Asian woman elected to the Los Angeles City Council and the first DSA member to win a seat on it. Today, Raman lives in the Silver Lake neighborhood with her husband, a television writer and producer whose credits include 30 Rock and Modern Family, and their twins. On the City Council, she has built her political profile around housing affordability, tenant protections and homelessness. She has pledged to cut the number of people living on Los Angeles streets by half before the city hosts the 2028 Olympic Games. Her relationship with the socialist organization, however, has never been straightforward. In 2020, Raman declared, "I absolutely do not support BDS," warning against close identification with a movement she said demonized Israel and Jewish people. After the October 7, 2023, Hamas massacre in Israel, she criticized a DSA statement that she believed lacked empathy for the victims. Her relationship with the organization deteriorated further when its local chapter reprimanded her for accepting support from a pro-Israel Democratic group. Her position on Israel has since shifted. Raman supported calls for a ceasefire in Gaza and, in an interview with political streamer Hasan Piker, said she believed Israel was committing genocide. At a gathering with Jewish voters in late September, she repeated that characterization, drawing visible disapproval from the audience. The local Jewish Federation described her remarks as crossing a red line. Raman sought to reassure the audience that she recognized Israel's right to exist and did not intend to make a boycott part of city policy. But a statement sent to the DSA this week went further than her previous public comments. "I believe the best way for working Angelenos to stand in solidarity with Gaza is through non-violent protest, legislative action, and diplomatic pressure, including BDS," Raman said. That language failed to satisfy the organization's national leadership, which is seeking a clearer personal commitment to the boycott movement. Raman has described the confrontation as internal political theater that should not distract Los Angeles residents from issues affecting their city. The dispute has also exposed tensions between the DSA's national leadership and its Los Angeles chapter. Local officials have defended their decision to endorse Raman and challenged the effort to overturn that endorsement. A difficult choice for Jewish voters in Los Angeles For many Israeli and Jewish residents of Los Angeles, the mayoral election presents what some describe as a political trap, a choice between imperfect candidates rather than a clear-cut decision. On one side is Bass, whose standing among parts of the Jewish community has suffered because of dissatisfaction with city management, her absence during the devastating wildfires and what critics describe as delayed responses to violent incidents and pro-Palestinian demonstrations on university campuses and outside synagogues. On the other is Raman, whose increasingly critical position toward Israel has raised concerns among some Jewish voters about the political direction of the city under her leadership. "She's our Mamdani," a Jewish resident of Beverly Hills told ynet, drawing a comparison between Raman and New York City's socialist mayor. The resident described the choice in stark terms: "Voters in this city now have the pleasure of choosing between complete incompetence from Mayor Bass and political radicalism from her challenger Raman. Good luck to all of us." Those views are not universal within the Jewish community, but they illustrate the political tension facing voters who are dissatisfied with Bass yet uncomfortable with Raman's positions on Israel. Obama steps in as another socialist faces a Senate test in Florida Across the country, another socialist candidate is confronting a different political challenge. Angie Nixon, 42, a Florida state representative from Jacksonville, is seeking to return a U.S. Senate seat to the Democrats for the first time since 2019. Unlike Raman, Nixon is not currently being asked to demonstrate her loyalty to the DSA, which she joined only this year and which has not formally endorsed her campaign. Her challenge lies instead with moderate voters, particularly within Florida's Jewish community. Nixon grew up in a poor Black neighborhood, raised by a mother who worked two jobs to support her children. She began her career as a labor organizer, established a bookstore and community center in Jacksonville, and became one of the most prominent Democratic critics of Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis. A charismatic campaigner who draws enthusiastic crowds at rallies, Nixon has focused on lowering living costs, expanding access to health care, housing and child care. Her positions on Israel, however, remain contentious. A month after the October 7 massacre, Nixon called for a ceasefire in Gaza during a session of the Florida House of Representatives. Many lawmakers turned their backs on her, and her proposal was defeated by a vote of 104 to 2. In August, Nixon achieved an upset in the Democratic Senate primary, defeating Alexander Vindman, the Jewish former military officer who became nationally known for his testimony during Donald Trump's first impeachment proceedings. Vindman had raised millions of dollars more than Nixon. Since then, several prominent Democrats have lined up behind her. Former President Barack Obama announced his endorsement last weekend, Sen. Bernie Sanders has appeared at campaign rallies in Florida, and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has publicly backed her candidacy. Nixon continues to accuse Israel of genocide and currently opposes U.S. military aid to the country. At the same time, she has intensified her efforts to engage with Jewish communities in recent months. Some Jewish Democrats in Florida say meetings with Nixon have changed their impressions of her, although they continue to struggle with her positions on Israel. Some acknowledge that they may vote for her despite their reservations because they cannot support the Republican alternative. Other Jewish activists view Nixon's opposition to Israeli government policy as a reason to support her and point to her relationships with both Jewish and Muslim communities. Unlike her unexpected victory in the Democratic primary, Nixon enters the general election trailing her Republican opponent in recent polls. Sen. Ashley Moody, who was appointed to the seat after Marco Rubio became secretary of state, received 50% support in a New York Times/Siena poll released Wednesday, compared with 44% for Nixon. Another recent survey showed Moody ahead by four percentage points. If Nixon wins, she would become the first Black woman to represent Florida in the U.S. Senate. For both Raman and Nixon, the approaching election poses a broader question for the American left: how candidates who have built their political identities around progressive activism navigate disagreements over Israel while seeking support from a much wider electorate.
news.summary: Democratic Socialists of America leaders demand that Nithya Raman endorse BDS and oppose arms shipments to Israel through LAX or risk losing their backing; a 40%-40% poll tie with Mayor Karen Bass leaves many Jewish voters facing a difficult choice

news.title: Forecaster Shifts 9 Senate Races as Nate Silver Touts Democratic Polling
news.text: Inside Elections has shifted nine Senate races on Thursday—all in favor of Democrats—as election forecaster Nate Silver highlighted "very strong polls" for the party, just days before the crucial midterm elections. Inside Elections shifted Georgia, Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, South Carolina, Louisiana and Mississippi's Senate races on Thursday. The changes come as Silver touted the favorable polling on X, saying, "Very strong polls for Democrats in individual Senate races over the past couple of days. Polls can be wrong, that's what models/probabilities/markets are for, but I think we're past the point where you can honestly say 'polls show the Senate is too close to call'." Midterm elections are commonly viewed as a test of the political environment facing the party in power, and the president's party has historically lost seats during them. President Donald Trump's overall approval rating and ranking on specific policy issues like the economy, immigration, jobs and the ongoing war in Iran have recently slipped as households across America are consistently flagging affordability concerns. The polling lows come as Trump has crisscrossed the country in the lead-up to November 3 to rally for potentially vulnerable GOP candidates. What To Know As Tuesday's election nears, Republicans are blitzing in an attempt to maintain their Senate majority. Trump administration officials including Vice President JD Vance and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. have also hit the campaign trail to stump for candidates in tight races. In its changes, Inside Elections has shifted some of the key Senate races that both Republicans and Democrats have tried to keep within their grasps. Below is a list of the shifts: Meanwhile, top election forecaster Cook Political Report lists Georgia's race as likely Democratic; Ohio, Texas, Kansas and Iowa's as toss-ups; South Carolina's as lean Republican; and Nebraska and Mississippi's as likely Republican. Cook rates Louisiana's Senate race as solid Republican. Silver Bulletin’s 2026 election Forecast with Leading Indicators, Polls and (Expert) Ratings (FLIPR) highlights Democratic polling leads with the caveat that Texas, Ohio, Alaska and Maine "are all just a normal-sized polling error away from flipping." The forecast also says there is a 77.7 percent chance that Democrats regain control of the Senate. On prediction market sites Kalshi and Polymarket, the Democratic Party has a double-digit lead for who will control the Senate following the midterms. news.title: ‘You Are Disgusting’: Trump Loses Cool At Reporter Over Health Questions
news.text:
US President Donald Trump on Thursday angrily confronted a reporter who questioned whether health concerns or exhaustion from his demanding campaign schedule had prompted him to cancel a planned rally in Kansas.
The exchange took place after the Republican National Committee (RNC) announced that two of Trump's remaining in-person campaign rallies, scheduled to be held in Kansas and Iowa, would no longer go ahead as planned.
Dismissing suggestions that his health or the strain of travelling had influenced the decision, Trump insisted that he was feeling well. He made the remarks after returning to Washington from a campaign trip to South Carolina.
Trump Calls Reporter ‘Disgusting’ Over Health Question
“You’re sick to ask that question. You are sick,” Trump told the reporter. “You’ve been following me for two weeks. I feel perfect. You are disgusting. Put yourself in shape. You look like hell.”
The US President's sharp response came amid questions about the cancellation of the planned rallies and whether his demanding schedule had begun taking a toll.
During a rally in South Carolina earlier, Trump had acknowledged that his packed schedule of campaign appearances had left him somewhat hoarse.
However, he rejected the suggestion that health concerns or campaign fatigue were behind the decision to abandon the Kansas event.
RNC Replaces Kansas, Iowa Rallies With Virtual Events
The RNC said the planned rallies in Kansas and Iowa would be replaced by a series of virtual campaign appearances, known as 'telerallies'.
According to the party, Trump would participate in a large number of such events across several states to support Republican candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
“With Republicans in a strong position in Kansas and Iowa, previously planned in-person rallies in those states will no longer take place as scheduled,” the RNC said in a statement.
Trump To Hold Final In-Person Rally In Florida
Following the changes, Trump's final in-person election rally is scheduled to take place in Florida on Friday.
The President also plans to campaign remotely for several Republican candidates as the midterm elections approach. Among those he intends to support is Kansas Senator Roger Marshall.
The shift to virtual appearances will allow Trump to continue campaigning for Republican candidates in multiple states without holding the previously scheduled in-person rallies.

news.title: North Korea’s Kim calls for rapid expansion of drone technology and observes weapons tests
news.text:
SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for rapidly expanding the country’s drone technology and observed tests of various weapons, state media reported Friday, as his nation remains embroiled in a standoff with rival South Korea along their heavily fortified border.

Acquiring advanced drones is a top priority for Kim, who now wants to beef up both conventional and nuclear capabilities. Experts say his troops dispatched to Russia to support its war against Ukraine have likely gained valuable expertise on drone warfare from Russian forces and related battlefield experiences.

The North’s official Korean Central News Agency said that Kim on Thursday visited an exhibition of a variety of attack and other drones that show recent achievements in the field of unmanned aeronautical technology.

In a speech at the exhibition, Kim stressed the need to seize “the absolute superiority in the drone technology” and announced unspecified steps needed to “rapidly expand and strengthen the unmanned aeronautical technology,” KCNA said.

To mark the event, KCNA said that North Korea later conducted test-launches of various drones, missiles and weapons from the 600 mm-caliber ultra-precision multiple rocket launchers. KCNA photos showed Kim watching soaring weapons or him clenching his fist while his teenage daughter was clapping her hands beside him. South Korea’s spy agency assesses that the girl, reportedly about 13, is likely Kim’s heir.

South Korea’s military earlier said it detected the launches of about 10 short-range ballistic missiles from North Korea’s eastern coastal town of Wonsan on Thursday. They were North Korea’s first ballistic weapons firings in 17 days.

Tensions between the two Koreas are running high since last month’s land mine blasts at their border that wounded three South Korean soldiers. Seoul accused North Korea of burying the mines south of the military demarcation line and demanded an apology. But Pyongyang has denied responsibility for the explosions and warned of retaliation if provoked.

Last week, North Korea threatened to resume propaganda loudspeaker broadcasts and place new weapons systems along the border.

North Korea has pulled out of talks with the US and South Korea after Kim’s high-stakes diplomacy with US President Donald Trump collapsed in 2019. In recent weeks, North Korea has dialed up weapons testing activities in a likely attempt to boost its leverage in potential diplomacy with the US after Trump expressed his eagerness to restore talks with Kim.

On Saturday, Kim made a surprise visit to a Chinese border town via a newly opened bridge and vowed to develop bilateral ties. Kim has recently taken steps to cement ties with China, North Korea’s economic pipeline, after years of prioritizing ties with Russia, including by supplying thousands of troops and ammunitions likely in return for economic and military assistance.

Meanwhile, Switzerland’s Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis arrived in North Korea on Thursday to see the reopening of Switzerland’s diplomatic office in Pyongyang and meet North Korean officials. He is travel on to South Korea on Friday.
news.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has emphasized the urgent need to enhance drone technology and has observed weapons tests, according to state media reports. The developments are part of efforts to strengthen North Korea’s military capabilities.

news.title: London, NATO may plan acts of sabotage against vessels with Russian diesel for US
news.text:
MOSCOW, October 30. /TASS/. The United Kingdom and NATO may be already preparing acts of sabotage against vessels that carry Russian diesel, Kremlin Aide, Chairman of the Russian Maritime Board Nikolay Patrushev said.

"Today, we can expect the most outrageous and skillfully organized provocations from the UK," Patrushev said in an interview with the Rossiiskaya Gazeta daily. "In particular, they will be directed against the Russia-US deal on diesel fuel supplies, which, of course, London does not approve of."

"I have no doubt that sabotage against tankers carrying Russian diesel is already being prepared in British and NATO headquarters," he noted.

According to Patrushev, Moscow is closely following developments of such risks.

"Unfortunately, Europeans today are unable to realize that they have pushed themselves into a corner with sanctions, geopolitical ventures and rampant Russophobia. They have burnt all bridges and don’t have a clue what to do now," he concluded.

Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump held a phone call on October 9, during which they discussed, among other things, petroleum product supplies. The Russian president said that Moscow had reiterated its readiness to supply oil and petroleum products to the United States and global markets.

According to Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak, Russia will lift its ban on diesel exports ahead of schedule and is ready to supply 300,000 tons of diesel in October, increasing the volume to 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons in December.

Monthly supplies could subsequently reach 3 million tons. The US administration, in turn, issued a general license authorizing Russian diesel supplies to the global market until April 7, 2027.

 Caribbean Cup success showcases strides in local club football, says Ricketts 







Kingston, Jamaica — Portmore United and Mount Pleasant Football Academy will contest the Concacaf Caribbean Cup final in December, ensuring that the regional crown will remain in Jamaican hands for the third time in four years.

It follows Portmore’s triumph in 2019 and the successes of fellow Jamaican clubs Cavalier in 2024 and Mount Pleasant in 2025.

Portmore and Mount Pleasant, having progressed to the final, also qualified for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.

It is the first time since 2004, when Harbour View faced Tivoli Gardens, that two Jamaican teams will meet in the final of the Caribbean club competition.

The Jamaica Football Federation (JFF), in congratulating both clubs, hailed their achievements as further evidence of the progress being made by local teams on the regional stage.

JFF President Michael Ricketts said the qualification of Portmore United and Mount Pleasant was a significant accomplishment for Jamaican football.

“I would like to wholeheartedly congratulate Mount Pleasant Football Academy and Portmore United for qualifying for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup and also for getting to the final of the Caribbean Cup,” Ricketts said.

“This is the fourth year in a row that at least one Jamaican club is in the final of the Caribbean Cup, so we are very pleased by the strides made by our clubs on the island,” he noted.

“This guarantees that just like in 2024 and in 2025, we will have a Jamaican club lift the Caribbean crown come December 5,” Ricketts added

The 2026 Caribbean Cup champions will receive a bye to the Round of 16 of the 2027 Champions Cup, while the runners-up and third-place team will begin their campaigns in the first round.

The official draw for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup is scheduled for Monday, December 21, 2026.

For Portmore United and Mount Pleasant, the immediate focus will be on securing regional bragging rights in December, with the added incentive of earning a more favourable route into next year’s continental competition.

news.title: Binance flags ‘potential security issue,’ says crypto firms froze more than $2.5 billion
news.text:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said Thursday it’s investigating reports of a potential security issue as its founder said the incident “does look like a hack on Binance.” The company said cryptocurrency firms had frozen more than $2.5 billion in funds by Thursday evening.

It wasn’t immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to accomplish and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been pilfered. The company said its teams are “working around the clock” to resolve the issue.

“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” a Binance spokesperson said in a statement.

“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” the statement continued.

The company wrote on its X account about two hours after its initial disclosure that the current verified total of frozen funds was $2.54 billion.

“This figure may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets,” the company wrote.

Binance also said all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while it conducts security checks, freezes funds and works with law enforcement.

Stablecoin providers Tether and Circle each said they froze funds Thursday in response to the incident.

Jeremy Allaire, co-founder and CEO of Circle, wrote on X that the company had frozen the equivalent of more than $800 million in currency associated with the incident “in coordination with law enforcement.” Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X that the company froze the equivalent of more than $1.5 billion in currency related to “a potential Binance exchange hack.”

The price of bitcoin dropped 3.2% Thursday evening to under $79,000.

Binance was founded in 2017 by Changpeng Zhao, who in 2023 pleaded guilty to a felony related to his failure to prevent money laundering on the platform and stepped down as CEO. President Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.

Zhao posted on X on Thursday that “User funds are safe!” but added that the incident “does look like a hack on Binance.” He added that while he doesn’t manage Binance anymore, “as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.”

news.title: Fired top Pentagon strategist accused of leaking Iran and Ukraine secrets – Axios
news.text:
The Pentagon’s former top military planner allegedly leaked classified information about Iran and Ukraine to journalists, Axios reported on Thursday, citing an internal investigation.

US War Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Staff earlier this week. Without mentioning Sylvia by name, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said on Thursday that the department had “zero tolerance for the intentional, unauthorized disclosure of classified information.” He added that the Pentagon “took necessary personnel action to protect sensitive information.”

According to Axios, Sylvia admitted to leaking information as early as June 2025, before most media outlets were barred from the Pentagon. He allegedly continued communicating with reporters through the encrypted messaging app Signal and once met a journalist at a diner to discuss military aid to Ukraine without authorization.

“He had trouble passing multiple polygraph interviews,” the report said, according to Axios.

Officials reportedly suspect that the general deliberately deleted records of his communications with a reporter while claiming the deletion was accidental. Sylvia also allegedly admitted to being a source for another story criticizing Pentagon leadership.

Sylvia’s departure comes amid reports that the US and Israel are preparing to resume strikes on Iran following next week’s US midterm elections. US President Donald Trump has indicated that he may take military action if Tehran refuses to accept his terms for a peace deal.

Since returning to the White House in early 2025, Trump has sought to crack down on government leaks, repeatedly accusing news outlets of conducting a smear campaign against him.

In July, Hegseth said the Pentagon and Justice Department had established a joint task force to “identify and prosecute leakers.”

In April 2025, Hegseth fired three senior Pentagon aides, Dan Caldwell, Darin Selnick and Colin Carroll, amid an investigation into alleged leaks of sensitive information to the media. All three denied wrongdoing, and none was subsequently charged with a crime. Caldwell later returned to the Trump administration in a position at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.

news.title: SA dangles chicken and pork concessions to the US for Agoa continuation
news.text:
Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition Parks Tau says South Africa has made “generous offers” to the US in a bid to continue its trade relationship with the world’s largest economy under the African Growth and Opportunity Act (Agoa).

Introduced by the US Congress in 2000, Agoa gives eligible African countries duty-free access to the US market for certain exports.

Since then, the programme has supported trade between Pretoria and the US, which remains a significant source of foreign direct investment for South Africa.

Speaking at a press briefing on Thursday, Tau was coy and reluctant to be drawn into the specific terms of SA’s offers to the US, saying only that they were in line with “our constitutional values and World Trade Organisation rules”.

He was speaking at a meeting of the National Economic Development and Labour Council (Nedlac), where representatives of government, business, labour and community organisations come together to negotiate the country’s economic, labour and development policy.

The partners are charting a way forward amid concerns that SA could be excluded from Agoa, with the eligibility review outcome from the US expected on 2 November.

South Africa exports vehicles, jewellery, ferroalloys, fruit and nuts, beverages and spirits to the US under Agoa.

The US, meanwhile, exports products including pork and poultry to South Africa – products that have become a negotiating tool and major point of contention in the ongoing negotiations between both nations.

Tau confirmed that SA’s offers relate to market access for poultry and pork. “The trade matters relate to pork and poultry and market access,” he said.

He explained that, as in any negotiation, countries need market access and animal health is important, including which parts can enter the country.

Issues around the treatment of some products would affect the outcome of the negotiations, he said.

Tau said South Africa had “made a set of offers” and met US officials in September 2026, but declined to disclose further details.

“We are awaiting a formal response [from the US] to the offer,” he said.

South Africa is however not prepared to make concessions to the US on various constitutional imperatives.

“There are non-negotiables in our negotiations. [Racial] transformation [imperatives] is a constitutional imperative and land reform operates within the Constitution. South Africa is open to practical engagements. These matters are best resolved through diplomatic and trade channels,” he said.

Read: Tau upbeat about Agoa’s continuation

The concern among the Nedlac partners around Agoa comes at a time when diplomatic tensions between Washington and Pretoria have intensified under US President Donald Trump’s administration, which claims that SA’s land policies discriminate against white people – a claim Pretoria rejects.

Agoa has been renewed twice since its introduction in 2000. The programme expired in September 2025 but was retroactively extended for one year in February 2026.

The US Congress has the final say on Agoa’s reauthorisation.

Under the notification process described in the programme, removing a country requires 60 days’ notice to Congress and the country concerned. For SA’s exclusion to take effect on 1 January, a decision would need to be announced by 2 November.

Tau recognises that Agoa has been good for South Africa.

An estimated 31% of South African exports to the US received duty-free access under the programme, amounting to $2.7 billion in 2021 and slightly more in subsequent years.

While Tau hopes South Africa will retain its Agoa benefits, he said the country must also strengthen existing trade relationships and develop new markets, particularly elsewhere in Africa.

He pointed to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which aims to create a single continental market and progressively reduce tariffs on goods traded between African countries.

Tau confirmed that his department is also exploring trade agreements with countries in the European Union, Asia, Canada, India and the Middle East.

“Diversification is not a rejection of the US. South Africa will be ready whatever is decided by the US. Our door to the US is open and our economy is resilient,” he said.

news.title: World News | Nvidia Chief Seen as Target of China Spy Plot: Report
news.text:
Washington, DC [US], October 30 (ANI): A top executive at a Singapore-based data centre firm named Megaspeed faced intense scrutiny over potential involvement in diverting advanced Nvidia AI chips towards China, as outlined in a report by The New York Times. US authorities reportedly determined that she operated as a Chinese intelligence asset, transmitting information back to Beijing.

According to the report, surveillance of the executive, identified as Chinese national Alice Huang or Huang Le, revealed that she maintained a close association with Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.

In what the publication described as a startling revelation, the report indicated that President Donald Trump had received briefings regarding the intelligence findings but opted against taking action. He remained cautious about disrupting Nvidia's chip sales, which continue to bolster economic growth and equity markets, and introducing further friction into commercial ties with Beijing.

Washington has consistently sought to prevent China from acquiring the technology necessary to match or surpass American capabilities in artificial intelligence. The discovery that Beijing was receiving information from an individual with direct access to Jensen Huang, who also maintains an alliance with President Trump, sparked major concerns within the White House.

Also Read | Patrick Stewart Dies at 86: Legendary Actor of 'Star Trek' and 'X-Men' Fame Suffered From Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.

The Nvidia chief executive successfully lobbied the administration during Trump's second term to reverse stricter export controls governing the company's chip shipments to China. He also finalised a deal with Trump permitting the US government to secure a 25 per cent stake in specific Nvidia processors authorised for sale to China.

As the Trump administration considered a comprehensive ban on Nvidia chip exports to China, Huang and his spouse travelled to Mar-a-Lago to persuade Trump to allow technology firms to continue doing business with Beijing.

Nvidia subsequently contributed upwards of USD 20 million towards Trump's ballroom fund, according to an individual familiar with the matter. The company also committed to spending USD 500 billion on domestic manufacturing infrastructure in the US.

The account of Alice Huang's operations is based on discussions with sources briefed on the surveillance efforts who spoke anonymously. The report noted that surveillance targeting Alice Huang continued and that enterprises previously linked to her had continued procuring Nvidia chips throughout the current year.

Nvidia asserted that it had previously dismissed allegations that Megaspeed was involved in smuggling chips to China. John Rizzo, a spokesperson for Nvidia, noted that clients such as Megaspeed "receive ordinary business information - not sensitive Nvidia trade secrets - and zero information relevant to national security".

Megaspeed is among the companies that purchase processors to build data centres before leasing computing capacity to enterprises operating within China.

The White House, the Central Intelligence Agency and the National Security Agency declined to comment. Alice Huang did not respond to inquiries seeking comment.

In a statement to The New York Times, Megaspeed indicated that its "current leadership" treats the situation "extremely seriously and is committed to getting to the facts behind allegations".

Liu Chang, spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington, stated that the US was pursuing a campaign of "groundless smears and slanders" directed at Beijing. (ANI)

news.title: Bitcoin market in chaos amid fears Binance cryptocurrency exchange hit by biggest hack in history
news.text:
Billions of dollars of cryptocurrency may have been stolen in what would be the market’s biggest ever hack, sending the bitcoin market into chaos.

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said on Thursday it had frozen $3 billion in crypto assets as it investigated a potential security breach. Stablecoin issuers Circle and Tether also froze assets thought to be related to the possible cyber attack.

"Binance will cover all hacking losses," Binance co-founder Yi He said, without providing more details about ⁠the incident.

The market impact of the possible hacking, which could be the largest-ever crypto heist according to analytics firm Chainalysis, was felt immediately in early Asian trading on Friday.

Bitcoin dropped about 2% to a six-week low of $77,646 and ether fell around 2% to a two-month low of $2,238.76. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binancefees, was down more than 8% over the past 24 hours at $694, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.

Crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8% while those of bitcoin buyer ⁠Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading.

Binance said the amount frozen could increase ​as ⁠it worked with law enforcement agencies, token issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and other industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.

Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the company, said in a post on X that the incident "looked like a hack."

Binance, which allows users to buy, ⁠sell and trade digital assets, has more than 335 million registered users globally and had about $160 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange's ​2024 annual report.

Binance runs a secure asset fund ‌for users, according to its website, which is a reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches.

"It's becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them, said Bernardo Brites, CEO of Trace Finance, ‌a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company.

"My view is that users will move away from smaller ‌and medium-sized exchanges, (it is) becoming too risky to park your money somewhere that couldn't cover a hack of meaningful size."

Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.

Binance said it was conducting security checks and would resume withdrawals once the issue was fully resolved. It added user funds remained safe and that teams were reviewing the incident.

The exchange ⁠also temporarily suspended trading on its Binance Alpha platform as a precaution.

World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said on Thursday it had worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack. Binance's Yi said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.

Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and was freezing affected funds and coordinating with relevant parties.

Miguel Morel, CEO of blockchain intelligence firm Arkham, said data indicated that billions of dollars appeared to ‌have been hacked from Binance by an unknown actor, though the exact cause had not been confirmed. Morel said the incident began around 4:30 ​p.m. EDT (2030 GMT) and appeared to be ongoing.

The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion ‌worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM ⁠Labs. In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry's vulnerability to hackers.

Authorities ⁠have warned that organised crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system.

Binance.US, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was not affected by the security incident.

Coinbase said ‌it was unaffected and was monitoring the situation.

In ​an unrelated incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market operator Polymarket temporarily halted trading ‌after a security incident involving a third-party provider. It later resumed trading ​and said it would fully reimburse affected traders.
news.summary: Billions of dollars worth of digital currency may have been stolen in suspect security breach at world’s biggest exchange
